baseline.name: Two simple copy loops for the two output halves
baseline.approach: Allocate 2n output slots, copy nums into the first half, then into the second.

archived.name: One loop writing both output halves
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary state plus O(n) returned storage

why: Combining the two loops changes control structure, not the amount of array data that must be produced.
quantitative_comparison: Both methods perform exactly 2n output writes and read the n source values as needed. The archive has n loop iterations rather than two n-iteration loops, but compiler optimization and memory behavior decide whether that matters. No speed or memory improvement is established.
tradeoffs: The one-loop version is compact; both allocate the same-sized result. Size arithmetic and allocation success are assumed.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
